text:
rafi: kicking off aurora-embed v0.9 onboarding. ran int4-per-tensor and saw a KR-focused recall@5 hit on short queries (<24 tok). any anisotropy flags? :thinking:
sam: dataset? short_korean_holdout?
rafi: yup. split kr/ar/en. fp16 kr recall@5=0.76 -> int4-per-tensor=0.62. int8-pc was 0.74.
priya: whoa that's big. what about cluster metrics?
rafi: umap shows kr clusters collapsing; within-kr cosine increases ~0.08, cross-lang separation shrinks. mean L2 norm for kr vectors up ~0.09.
zhao: sounds like a few dims dominate after quantization. did you try post-quant L2 renorm?
rafi: did. post-l2 norm bumped recall@5 to 0.69 only. still down.
sam: try pre-whiten PCA before quant to spread variance. also test clamp_percentile changes.
rafi: current quant snippet:
```
quant:
  dtype: int4
  scheme: per_tensor
  symmetric: true
  clamp_percentile: 0.99
  calibrate_batches: 512
```
rafia: queued pre-whiten + post-l2 + ef=200 reindex. cmd: `./evals/run_eval.sh --model aurora-v0.9 --quant int4-pertensor --dataset short_korean_holdout --prewhiten true --postnorm l2 --knn hnsw --ef 200`
priya: also upload failing sample diffs; useful to inspect tokens/topics that flip.
rafi: uploaded diffs -> s3://redwood-evals/aurora/int4_kr_diffs.csv
zhao: check tokenizer behavior — short kr queries could have more subword artifacts shifting embedding scale.
rafi: token stats match across fp16 and quant runs. no big differences.
sam: if pre-whiten helps, that points to eigendirection dominance. could add simple preproc step for int4 pipelines.
rafi: preliminary: pre-whiten + post-l2 recovered recall@5 to 0.73. still ~0.03 under fp16.
priya: try stochastic rounding or bias-correction if supported. offset-correct (fp16 mean - quant mean) is a quick diagnostic too.
rafi: quant lib flags: `--stochastic` and `--bias-correct`. I'll try bias-correct + asymmetric next.
eval-bot: job queued job_id=2026_03_23_aurora_int4_01 docs=32k langs=[kr,ar,en] metrics=[recall@1,recall@5,cosine_gap,cluster_purity,mean_norm]
zhao: another check: run per-channel int4 (if supported) vs per-tensor to see whether per-channel reduces bias on specific dims.
sam: be mindful of index ef and reindex variance — increase ef to 256 to rule that out.
rafi: will run bias-correct + asymmetric + ef=256. thanks. if that recovers, recommend pre-whiten + bias-correct for KR-heavy routes and mark int4-per-tensor opt-in for KR customers.
priya: add a CI smoke test that runs short_korean_holdout and gates onboarding if recall@5 drops >0.04 vs fp16. also collect 200 probe KR queries for continuous monitoring.
rafi: will draft the note and file follow-up ticket for dim-bias mitigation. thanks all. :thumbsup:
